raised.quote:
if (!allowedKeys.has(verdict.new_issue_key!)) { skipped++; continue; }
      pushInto(byKey, verdict.new_issue_key!, verdict);
raised.claim: Verdicts attached to newly proposed issues are not checked against those issues' scopes.
raised.why_it_breaks: A zero-candidate row referencing a new issue scoped to candidates_count > 0 is filed and recorded even though the issue's own scope contradicts the row.

raised.quote:
if (scope.beer_ids.length > 0) return true;
  return scope.where.some((t) => t.col !== 'review_class');
raised.claim: Adding any beer ID makes a whole-class where scope legal.
raised.why_it_breaks: A scope with beer_ids [1] and where review_class = matcher_bug passes legality, and the OR evaluation subsequently accepts every matcher_bug row, recreating the whole-class dumping ground the guard is meant to prevent.

raised.claim: The saturation guard does not count other attachments accepted in the same plan.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an issue already has 11 post-creation rows and a batch proposes 20 matching rows, each verdict sees the unchanged count of 11 and all 20 are attached instead of stopping at 12.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: The saturation count loses previously attached rows when their failure records are cleared or re-triaged.
raised.why_it_breaks: After an issue reaches 12 attachments, a beer matching deletes its enrich_failures row, or a candidate-count transition clears reviewed_at; the count drops below 12 and the issue accepts further attachments despite its existing comment history.

raised.claim: Model-authored issue prose can override the structured scope parsed on the next run.
raised.why_it_breaks: If issue.body contains an earlier fenced triage-scope block, parseScopeBlock takes that first block rather than the appended block; a valid but different scope silently changes which future rows are accepted, while a malformed block makes the issue unscoped.

raised.claim: Appending the scope after unrestricted issue prose can hide it from the model on subsequent runs.
raised.why_it_breaks: When issue.body is at least 2,000 characters, buildTriagePrompt truncates the body before the appended scope, so the model routes without seeing the predicate and the deterministic guard can repeatedly reject otherwise avoidable misroutes.

raised.claim: Guard-hit counters are not logged when the model returns a verdict for every row.
raised.why_it_breaks: If every orphan has a verdict but every attachment is rejected by scope or saturation, covered still equals the batch size, so no guardHits log is emitted and repeated guard failures remain invisible.

raised.claim: Degraded absence verdicts are reported as wontfix in the daily outcome.
raised.why_it_breaks: This adds matcher_bug verdicts to plan.quiet, but the job increments wontfix for every quiet verdict that is not not_on_untappd, so an unprobed absence appears in the digest as a wontfix even though the database records matcher_bug.

raised.quote:
UPDATE enrich_failures
     SET issue_number = CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER)
   WHERE review_note LIKE '%→ #%'
     AND CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER) > 0;
raised.claim: The migration backfills the first issue reference in a note rather than the appended routing reference.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a model note such as 'related to → #123 → #347', where #347 is the actual appended target, the migration records issue_number 123 and attributes the row and saturation count to the wrong issue.

raised.quote: ALTER TABLE enrich_failures ADD COLUMN issue_number INTEGER;
raised.claim: The new authoritative issue link is not cleared when an existing failure is reopened for triage.
raised.why_it_breaks: When recordEnrichFailure observes a candidates_count boundary transition, it clears review_class, review_note and reviewed_at but leaves issue_number intact, so an untriaged row continues to report its old issue as its authoritative link.

raised.claim: The strict tool schema permits scope terms that the analysis parser rejects.
raised.why_it_breaks: A tool response containing, for example, candidates_count with op '=' and value null satisfies this JSON schema but fails ScopeTermSchema, causing the entire analysis to fail instead of producing a guarded plan.
